answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable. Consider a marble as the anchor of the cost.
